items.title: Why does StoreKit return USD pricing in TestFlight but EUR in development builds on the same iPhone?
items.body:
I'm experiencing a reproducible StoreKit pricing inconsistency in a Flutter iOS application using a non-consumable In-App Purchase.

App Store Connect configuration:

  • Product type: Non-consumable

  • Bulgarian storefront price: EUR 6.99

  • US storefront price: USD 5.99

  • Test device: Same physical iPhone with Bulgarian storefront

  • TestFlight build: 22

Observed behavior:

Installation methodDisplayed priceStandalone development-signed StoreKit 2 probeEUR 6.99 (correct)Full Flutter app, release mode, development-signedEUR 6.99 (correct)Full Flutter app installed through TestFlightUSD 5.99 (incorrect)Native Apple purchase confirmation sheet in TestFlightEUR 6.99 (correct)

The Flutter app displays the localized price returned by StoreKit without manually converting currencies or hardcoding prices.

Both development-signed builds return the correct Bulgarian price.

However, installing the TestFlight version immediately reproduces the incorrect USD price, even though Apple's native purchase confirmation sheet correctly shows EUR 6.99.

Steps to reproduce:

  1. Configure a non-consumable In-App Purchase with different prices for Bulgaria and the United States.

  2. Install the development-signed Flutter application on an iPhone using the Bulgarian storefront.

  3. Confirm that the displayed price is EUR 6.99.

  4. Install the TestFlight build of the same application.

  5. Observe that the app displays USD 5.99.

  6. Initiate the purchase and observe that Apple's native confirmation sheet displays EUR 6.99.

Expected behavior:

The application should display EUR 6.99 in both development-signed and TestFlight installations.

Actual behavior:

Only the TestFlight installation displays USD 5.99.

items.title: How do I safely remove unused asyncio locks without causing duplicate requests?
items.body:
I'm using asyncio.Lock() to prevent multiple requests for the same user from running at the same time.

I also want to remove locks when they're no longer needed instead of keeping them in memory indefinitely.

Here's a simplified version of what I'm doing:

import asyncio

locks = {}

async def send_request(user_id):
    print(f"Starting request for {user_id}")
    await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    print(f"Finished request for {user_id}")

async def process(user_id):
    lock = locks.setdefault(user_id, asyncio.Lock())

    async with lock:
        if user_id in locks:
            del locks[user_id]

        await send_request(user_id)

async def main():
    first = asyncio.create_task(process(42))
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)

    second = asyncio.create_task(process(42))
    await asyncio.gather(first, second)

asyncio.run(main())

The output is:

Starting request for 42
Starting request for 42
Finished request for 42
Finished request for 42

Both requests start before either one finishes, which is what I'm trying to avoid.

I understand that deleting the lock from the dictionary doesn't release it for tasks already using it. The issue is that another task can create a new lock for the same user while the old one is still active.

How can I safely remove unused locks without allowing two different locks to exist for the same user at the same time?

I'd prefer not to keep a lock for every user indefinitely, especially when the number of user IDs can grow over time.

items.title: Sanity check on my hybrid RAG settings, and pgvector vs OpenSearch/Elasticsearch?
items.body:
I'd love a quick review of my RAG retrieval settings and some advice on the vector store.

Current stack

  • Backend: FastAPI (Python) with Docker workers for ingestion

  • Vector DB: ChromaDB (one collection per project)

  • Keyword search: PostgreSQL full-text search (tsvector, ts_rank_cd)

  • Cache: Redis

  • Embeddings: Mistral, OpenAI, Jina (via Ollama)

  • LLMs: OpenAI, Mistral, Gemini

  • Reranker: BAAI/bge-reranker-base

  • Chunking: LlamaIndex SentenceSplitter

Indexing

  • Chunks of 1,000–1,500 characters with 200 overlap. Tables are split by whole rows.

  • A title/breadcrumb header (up to 200 characters) is added before embedding.

  • Normalized embeddings with cosine distance.

Retrieval

  • sim=1−d\text{sim} = 1 - dsim=1−d, with threshold τ=0.3\tau = 0.3τ=0.3 (range 0.2–0.45). If nothing passes, retry at 0.5τ0.5\tau0.5τ.

  • Small collections (300 chunks or fewer): score=0.65⋅sim+0.35⋅kw\text{score} = 0.65 \cdot \text{sim} + 0.35 \cdot \text{kw}score=0.65⋅sim+0.35⋅kw

  • Large collections: RRF, score=∑w/(60+rank)\text{score} = \sum w / (60 + \text{rank})score=∑w/(60+rank). Vector, keyword and exact-ID lists each have w=1w = 1w=1, and structured records have w=2w = 2w=2.

  • Results found only by keyword search are kept if sim≥0.75×\text{sim} \ge 0.75 \timessim≥0.75× the best vector similarity.

Reranking

  • Reranks the top 30 within an 800 ms budget, reading up to 256 tokens per chunk, with d=1−σ(s)d = 1 - \sigma(s)d=1−σ(s).

  • Skipped when the top result has sim≥0.75\text{sim} \ge 0.75sim≥0.75 and leads the second by at least 0.10.

Final context

  • top-k = 5, with near-duplicates removed and at most 3 chunks per page.

  • Confidence requires top-1 similarity of at least 0.16 and a top-3 average of at least 0.20. Otherwise it retries with the original query.

Questions

  1. Is a weighted mix for small collections and RRF for large ones sensible, or should I use one method everywhere?

  2. Are 256 tokens per chunk too few for bge-reranker-base when chunks are about 1,400 characters?

  3. Are the confidence floors (0.16 / 0.20) too low for production?

  4. Since keyword search already runs in Postgres, would you move vectors to Postgres + pgvector, or switch to OpenSearch / Elasticsearch for native hybrid search (BM25 plus vectors) at multi-tenant scale? Which works better in production?

Thanks!

        for entry in feed.entries:
            articles.append({
                "title": entry.title,
                "link": entry.link,
                "published": getattr(entry, "published", "")
            })

    return articles

def analyse_article(text):

            }
        )

        result = response.json()["response"]

    except Exception as e:

        return ""

def already_seen(url):

        (url,)

    return cur.fetchone() is not None

def save_article(article, analysis):
    conn.execute(

        """,
        (
            article["link"],
            article["title"],
            analysis["company"],
            analysis["ticker"],
            analysis["score"],
            analysis["summary"],
            analysis["catalyst"],
            analysis["risk"],
            analysis["published"]
        )
    )

def run():
    articles = get_articles()
    for article in articles:
        if already_seen(article["link"]):

        print(f"Analyzing article: {article['title']}")

        analysis = analyse_article(text)

        if not analysis['relevant']:

if __name__ == "__main__":

items.title: Tableau: Latitude/ Longitude fields from Geographic Role cannot be referenced in a calculated field (MAKEPOINT, DISTANCE, etc.))
items.body:
I have a field with Geographic Role set to ZIP Code (right-click field → Geographic Role → Zip Code/Postcode). This works fine for building a map such as dragging the ZIP field onto a worksheet correctly auto-populates Latitude (generated) and Longitude (generated) onto the Rows/Columns shelves, and the map renders correctly.

The problem: I need to use those same generated coordinates inside a calculated field — specifically to compute distance between two points using MAKEPOINT() / DISTANCE(). I cannot get this to work:

  • Typing [Latitude (generated)] directly into the calculated field editor returns “Reference to undefined field”, even though the field renders correctly on an actual worksheet.

  • The field does not appear in the calculated-field editor’s autocomplete dropdown when I start typing Lat.

  • With the calculated field editor open, double-clicking Latitude (generated) in the Data pane (where it’s clearly listed and usable elsewhere) does not insert anything into the formula box.

This is on Tableau Desktop 2024.3 connected via Custom SQL via Amazon Athena connector, with two logical tables joined via a Relationship in the same data source.

What I’m trying to accomplish: calculate the distance between two geocoded points that originate from two different tables in the same data source (e.g., MAKEPOINT([Table A Latitude], [Table A Longitude]) compared against MAKEPOINT([Table B Latitude], [Table B Longitude])).

What I already know as a workaround (and am trying to avoid if possible): building a temporary worksheet with the ZIP field on it, selecting all marks, using “View Data” → “Export All” to dump the generated coordinates to a CSV, then re-importing that CSV as a new data source and joining it back on the plain ZIP text field. This works, but requires re-running it manually every time new ZIP codes show up in the underlying data, which isn’t sustainable for a dashboard that’s supposed to refresh automatically.

Question: Is there a supported way to reference Geographic-Role-generated Latitude/Longitude fields directly inside a calculated field without this export/re-import workaround? Is this a documented/intentional Tableau limitation, and if so, is there a cleaner pattern others use for cross-table distance calculations when both sides’ coordinates come from ZIP-code geocoding?

items.title: How can I invalidate existing Firebase Auth password reset OOB codes?
items.body:
We are implementing a custom password recovery flow using Firebase Authentication with Identity Platform.

Our security requirement is that password recovery must only be completed from a previously registered and approved browser.

We have implemented a custom recovery mechanism using short-lived, single-use recovery tickets and server-side verification of the approved browser credential.

However, we discovered that previously issued Firebase PASSWORD_RESET OOB codes may bypass this custom recovery flow.

Environment:

  • Firebase Authentication with Identity Platform
  • Firebase Admin SDK for Node.js
  • Cloud Functions Gen2
  • Email/password authentication

What we tested:

  1. We deployed a beforeSendEmail blocking function.

  2. New public PASSWORD_RESET requests were successfully blocked.

  3. Admin-generated password reset links were also blocked.

  4. However, a PASSWORD_RESET OOB code issued before enabling the blocking function could still be consumed successfully through accounts.resetPassword.

  5. Calling revokeRefreshTokens() did not invalidate an already issued PASSWORD_RESET OOB code.

  6. Updating the user's password through Firebase Admin SDK also did not invalidate an already issued PASSWORD_RESET OOB code.

All tests were performed using an authorized test account in an isolated Firebase project.

We need to safely migrate from Firebase's built-in password reset mechanism to our custom recovery flow.

My questions are:

  1. What is the documented maximum lifetime of a Firebase Authentication PASSWORD_RESET OOB code?

  2. Do password reset codes generated through the public sendOobCode API and Admin SDK generatePasswordResetLink() have the same expiration period?

  3. Is there a supported API or administrative operation that invalidates all outstanding PASSWORD_RESET OOB codes for a specific user or Firebase project?

  4. If no such invalidation API exists, what is the recommended migration strategy to ensure previously issued OOB codes cannot bypass a newly enforced password recovery policy?

  5. Does Firebase provide any supported configuration to control the expiration time of PASSWORD_RESET OOB codes?

We are specifically looking for documented Firebase / Identity Platform behavior rather than an assumed expiration duration.

Any official documentation or Firebase team clarification would be greatly appreciated.

items.title: How can I conduct (and plot) a chisquare test for pairwise combinations of three variables?
items.body:
I have data from a series of behavioral choice tests where I offered my test subjects (ladybugs) each combination of three substances: A, B, and C (that is, AB, BC, and AC). I want to evaluate if they had a preference for each combination (A vs B, B vs C, and A vs C) via three chi-square tests. Unfortunately, I am having trouble performing chisq tests in R using chisq.test because it can't handle NA values (I get the error "all entries of 'x' must be nonnegative and finite"), but I worry that doing three separate chisq tests would be dubious because I couldn't correct for multiple comparisons, not to mention that it would make it more difficult to plot. I can arrange my data such that there are no NAs (see longdata), but then it isn't formatted as a contingency table. Any help would be greatly appreciated!

# make contingency table
data <- matrix(c(9,10,NA,8,NA,12,NA,9,6),ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
rownames(data) <- c('A','B','C')
colnames(data) <- c('AB','AC','BC')
data <- as.data.frame(data)

# format differently so i can plot it
longdata <- matrix(c('A','AB',9,
                     'B','AB',10,
                     'A','AC',8,
                     'C','AC',12,
                     'B','BC',9,
                     'C','BC',6),nrow = 6,byrow = TRUE)
colnames(longdata) <- c('liquid','assay','count')
longdata <- as.data.frame(longdata)

#the plot (sans p-values)
ggplot(data = longdata, aes(assay, count, fill = liquid)) + 
  geom_col(position = "dodge")

This is the look of the plot I'm going for, with pairwise statistical tests representing each assay, but since I was able compare means, I didn't need to run chisquare tests, avoiding the issue I'm having above.

items.title: React router 8 importing @react-router/dev/routes in production build
items.body:
I want to deploy a react router 8 app with docker. This is my package.json (showing only react router's related stuff)

{
 "scripts": {
    "build": "react-router build",
    "start": "react-router-serve ./build/server/index.js",
  },
 "dependencies": {
    "@react-router/node": "^8.4.0",
    "@react-router/serve": "^8.4.0",
    "react-router": "^8.4.0",
    "react": "^19.3.0",
    "react-dom": "^19.3.0",
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@react-router/dev": "^8.4.0",
    "@tailwindcss/vite": "^4.3.3",
    "typescript": "^7.0.2",
    "vite": "^8.3.0"
  },
}

My react-router.config.ts:

import type { Config } from '@react-router/dev/config';

export default {
  ssr: true,
} satisfies Config;

and my vite.config.ts:

import { reactRouter } from '@react-router/dev/vite';
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig({
  resolve: {
    tsconfigPaths: true,
  },
  plugins: [tailwindcss(), reactRouter()],
});

Everything is very similar to the official template https://github.com/remix-run/react-router-templates/tree/main/default

Both the official template and I are omitting development dependencies from the final image. They do npm ci --omit=dev and I run npm prune --omit=dev after build. I am kinda sure that they both result in the same thing, and I am doing the latter just to save some bandwidth... Anyway, this doesn't seem to be the original problem. The broken thing is that react router docs explicitly says:

The React Router CLI comes from the @react-router/dev package. Make sure it is in your package.json devDependencies so it doesn't get deployed to your server.

But the built file imports it (!):

# build/server/index.js
...
import { index, layout, prefix, route } from "@react-router/dev/routes";
...

A quick fix will be adding @react-router/dev to dependencies rather than devDependencies (or stop pruning dev deps from final build, because build works locally when all packages are available). But this feels illegal, and I don't want to fix it that way.

Is it a bug in react-router (& is it supposed to convert routes and use another package?), or it's the documentation being misleading, or is it me using the package wrongly?

To give more context, I have many routes.ts files using this pattern:

import { index, layout, prefix, route } from '@react-router/dev/routes';

export const settings = [
  ...prefix('settings', [
    layout('./settings/layout.tsx', [
      index('./settings/page.tsx'),
      route('app', './settings/app/page.tsx'),
    ]),
  ]),
];

items.title: Why does recv() and write() get slower the more work is done between subsequent calls?
items.body:
I'm trying to set up a low-latency TCP communication channel, but while profiling, I noticed an odd behavior, which I was able to reduce to the following setup:

The simplified structure of the client program is:


write()
wait_for_n_usecs(n)
read()

and for the server it is:

read()
wait_for_n_usecs(n)
write()

However, I noticed that as you increase n, both the time attributed to write() and the time attributed to read() also increase (though the rate of increase for write is lower than for read).

Some numbers:
When n=5:
    On macOS 11:
         Read time: 32 ms
         Write time: 2 ms
     On Linux 7.2.9:
         Read time: 119 ms
         Write time: 18 ms
When n=50000:
    On macOS 11:
         Read time: 219 ms
         Write time: 12 ms
     On Linux 7.2.9:
        Read time: 153 ms
        Write time: 35 ms

// backend.cpp
#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <netinet/in.h>
#include <netinet/tcp.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <csignal>
#include <cerrno>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <chrono>

#define SIZE 20
#define TIMES 256*4

static void die(const char* what){ perror(what); exit(1); }

// Read exactly n bytes (handles partial reads / EINTR)
static void read_all(int fd, uint8_t* buf, size_t n){
    size_t got = 0;
    while(got < n){
        ssize_t r = ::read(fd, buf + got, n - got);
        if(r > 0) got += (size_t)r;
        else if(r == 0){ fprintf(stderr, "peer closed connection\n"); exit(1); }
        else if(errno != EINTR) die("read");
    }
}

// Write exactly n bytes (handles partial writes / EINTR)
static void write_all(int fd, const uint8_t* buf, size_t n){
    size_t sent = 0;
    while(sent < n){
        ssize_t w = ::write(fd, buf + sent, n - sent);
        if(w >= 0) sent += (size_t)w;
        else if(errno != EINTR) die("write");
    }
}

uint8_t test_buf[SIZE];
uint8_t actual_buf[SIZE];
std::chrono::nanoseconds diff(0);
std::chrono::microseconds read_time(0);
std::chrono::microseconds write_time(0);
std::chrono::nanoseconds time_diff(0);

int main(int argc, char** argv){
    signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN);

    int listen_fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
    if(listen_fd < 0) die("socket");

    int one = 1;
    setsockopt(listen_fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, &one, sizeof(one));

    sockaddr_in addr{};
    addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    addr.sin_port = htons(9000);
    if(inet_pton(AF_INET, "127.0.0.1", &addr.sin_addr) != 1) die("inet_pton");

    if(bind(listen_fd, (sockaddr*)&addr, sizeof(addr)) < 0) die("bind");
    if(listen(listen_fd, 1) < 0) die("listen");

    int client = accept(listen_fd, nullptr, nullptr);
    if(client < 0) die("accept");

    setsockopt(client, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_NODELAY, &one, sizeof(one));

    auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

    for(int i=0; i < TIMES; i++){
        auto start1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        memset(test_buf, i, SIZE);
        auto end1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        diff+=(end1 - start1);

        start1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        read_all(client, actual_buf, SIZE);
        end1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        read_time+=std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::microseconds>(end1-start1);

        #if 1 //Verification of transmission integrity
        start1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        if (memcmp(test_buf, actual_buf, SIZE)){
            printf("Buffers don't match!\n");
            printf("Offending: %i\n", i);
            exit(1);
        }
        end1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        diff+=(end1 - start1);
        #endif

        start1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        #if 1
        {
            auto s = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
            while((std::chrono::steady_clock::now()-s) < std::chrono::microseconds(50000)){}
        }
        #else
        {
            volatile uint64_t j =0;
            for (uint64_t k=0; k < 5*58315; k++) j++;
        }
        #endif
        end1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        time_diff+=(end1 - start1);

        start1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        write_all(client, actual_buf, SIZE);
        end1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        write_time+=std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::microseconds>(end1-start1);
    }

    auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    const auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>((end - start)-diff-time_diff);

    uint64_t transfer_size = TIMES*SIZE*2ULL;
    uint64_t transfer_time = duration.count();

    printf("Busy-wait Duration: %lld us\n", (long long)(time_diff.count()/1000));
    printf("Time to complete: %llu ms\n", (unsigned long long)transfer_time);
    printf("Approximate throughput: %llu GB/s\n", (unsigned long long)((transfer_size/transfer_time)/1000000));

    printf("Read time: %llu ms\n", (unsigned long long)std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(read_time).count());
    printf("Write time: %llu ms\n", (unsigned long long)std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(write_time).count());

    close(client);
    close(listen_fd);
}

// client.cpp
#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <netinet/in.h>
#include <netinet/tcp.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <csignal>
#include <cerrno>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <chrono>

#define SIZE 20
#define TIMES 256*4

static void die(const char* what){ perror(what); exit(1); }

static void read_all(int fd, uint8_t* buf, size_t n){
    size_t got = 0;
    while(got < n){
        ssize_t r = ::read(fd, buf + got, n - got);
        if(r > 0) got += (size_t)r;
        else if(r == 0){ fprintf(stderr, "peer closed connection\n"); exit(1); }
        else if(errno != EINTR) die("read");
    }
}

static void write_all(int fd, const uint8_t* buf, size_t n){
    size_t sent = 0;
    while(sent < n){
        ssize_t w = ::write(fd, buf + sent, n - sent);
        if(w >= 0) sent += (size_t)w;
        else if(errno != EINTR) die("write");
    }
}

uint8_t test_buf[SIZE];
uint8_t actual_buf[SIZE];
std::chrono::nanoseconds diff(0);
std::chrono::nanoseconds time_diff(0);

int main(int argc, char** argv){
    signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN);

    int client = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
    if(client < 0) die("socket");

    sockaddr_in addr{};
    addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    addr.sin_port = htons(9000);
    if(inet_pton(AF_INET, "127.0.0.1", &addr.sin_addr) != 1) die("inet_pton");

    if(connect(client, (sockaddr*)&addr, sizeof(addr)) < 0) die("connect");

    int one = 1;
    setsockopt(client, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_NODELAY, &one, sizeof(one));

    auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

    for(int i=0; i < TIMES; i++){
        auto start1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        memset(test_buf, i, SIZE);
        auto end1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        diff+=(end1 - start1);

        write_all(client, test_buf, SIZE);

        start1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        #if 1
        {
            auto s = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
            while((std::chrono::steady_clock::now()-s) < std::chrono::microseconds(50000)){}
        }
        #else
        {
            volatile uint64_t j =0;
            for (uint64_t k=0; k < 5*58315; k++) j++;
        }
        #endif
        end1=std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        time_diff+=(end1-start1);

        read_all(client, actual_buf, SIZE);

        #if 1 //Verification of transmission integrity
        if (memcmp(test_buf, actual_buf, SIZE)){
            printf("Buffers don't match!\n");
            printf("Offending: %i\n", i);
            exit(1);
        }
        #endif
    }

    auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    const auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>((end - start) - diff - time_diff);

    uint64_t transfer_size = TIMES*SIZE*2ULL;
    uint64_t transfer_time = duration.count();

    printf("Diff: %lld us\n", (long long)(time_diff.count()/1000));
    printf("Time to complete: %llu ms\n", (unsigned long long)transfer_time);
    printf("Approximate throughput: %llu GB/s\n", (unsigned long long)((transfer_size/transfer_time)/1000000));

    close(client);
}

Both were compiled with clang++ -std=c++20 -O3

items.title: Is there any disadvantage to calling document.createElement with the “wrong” document?
items.body:
Any time you call document.createElement (or its cousins, e.g. createDocumentFragment), the new node belongs to that document. It's my understanding that if you add that new node to a different document, then it will be updated to belong to that other document, and everything will work fine.

I'm writing a factory function that creates elements given tag type, attributes, and children. I would rather not have to pass the document in as a parameter.

In a situation where there are multiple documents pertaining to an application (e.g. an iframe, or a child window), if all you're doing is creating new nodes and adding them to some document, is there any disadvantage to creating all of those nodes on the topmost document? E.g. are there any semantic differences, or performance costs?

items.title: With the latest version of SQL Server installed... why is SSMS still using an old one?
items.body:
Here is the latest version of my stored procedure:

USE [IncomeExpense]
GO

SET ANSI_NULLS ON  
GO  
SET QUOTED_IDENTIFIER ON  
GO  

DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS dbo.ExpensesByMonth  
GO  

CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.ExpensesByMonth  
    @first varchar(10),  
    @last  varchar(10) = NULL
AS  
BEGIN  
    SET NOCOUNT ON;  

    DECLARE @dfirst DATE,  
            @dlast DATE;  

    PRINT CONCAT( 'LENGTH Of FIRST IS ', LEN(@first) );  

    IF LEN(@first) = 10  
    BEGIN               
        SET @dfirst = CONVERT(DATE, @first, 120);  
    END;  
    ELSE IF LEN(@first) = 7  
    BEGIN                     
        SET @dfirst = CONVERT(DATE, @first + '-01', 120);       
    END;  
    ELSE
    BEGIN  
        RAISERROR('The start date format is invalid', 16, 1) WITH NOWAIT; 
        RETURN;  
    END;            

    IF @last IS NULL
    BEGIN           
        SET @dlast = EOMONTH(@dfirst)  
    END                                                     
    ELSE IF LEN(@last) = 7                               
    BEGIN                                                  
        SET @dlast = EOMONTH(@last + '-01')  
    END;  
    ELSE
    BEGIN  
        RAISERROR('The end date format is invalid', 16, 1) WITH NOWAIT;  
        RETURN;  
    END;            

    SELECT 
        Category,  
        FORMAT(SUM(Amount), 'C', 'en-US'),  
        FORMAT(SUM(CASE WHEN Regular = 'Y' THEN Amount ELSE 0 END), 'C', 'en-US')  
    FROM 
        IncomeExpense.dbo.IncomeExpense  
    WHERE 
        Date BETWEEN @dfirst AND @dlast  
    GROUP BY 
        Category                                       
END;

My original problem was that SQL Server said the DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS statement was invalid. I found that I was using SSMS 2022 with SQL Server 2014, which doesn't support that statement.

I installed the latest versions of both SSMS and SQL Server. Then I tried to run the procedure again, and got the same error. I found that SSMS was still using SQL Server 2014.

I found instructions that told me that to change the version of SQL Server SSMS uses, I should reconnect to SQL Server and specify the new version in the connection dialog. I did that, then I tried to run the procedure, and I got the same error. SELECT @@VERSION says that SSMS is still using SQL Server 2014.

The SQL Server installer told me that it was updating SSMS 21 and installing SQL Server 2022. It didn't say anything about SQL Server 2014, although I know I was running 2014 before. Now the connection dialog shows that I've selected SSMS 22 instead of SSMS 21, and SSMS is still using SQL Server 2014.

How can I fix this?

items.title: Shifting an atomic store to a non-temporal vector instruction bypass the CPU's Store Buffer forwarding, causing a relaxed load to stall
items.body:
I am working on a ultra low latency ring buffer in C++20 on an Intel Ice Lake (x86_64) architecture. I am trying to optimize the producer thread's throughput by minimizing cache pollution when writing large blocks of telemetry data, before signaling the consumer thread via a std::atomic<uint64_64> sequence counter.

Normally, the release-store sequence looks like this:

// thread 1 (Producer)
std::memcpy(shared_buffer, local_data, 64); // Write 64 bytes
ring_buffer_tail.store(new_tail, std::memory_order_release);

I replaced the standard std::memcpy with AVX-512 non-temporal vector stores (_mm512_stream_si512) to bypass the L1/L2 caches and write directly to main memory (Write-Combining memory type behavior).

// optimized thread 1 (Producer)
_mm512_stream_si512(reinterpret_block, vector_data); // Non-temporal store
ring_buffer_tail.store(new_tail, std::memory_order_release);

std::memory_order_release makes sure that all previous writes (including the non-temporal vector store) are visible to another thread once that thread acquires the atomic variable.

On x86_64, standard atomic stores are compiled into a simple MOV instruction because the hardware memory model is strongly ordered (Total Store Order / TSO).

BUT, during high-frequency micro-benchmarking using hardware performance counters (perf), I noticed a massive 300-cycle stall on the very next local, completely unrelated relaxed load (std::memory_order_relaxed) executed by the same producer thread.

If I switch back to standard std::memcpy, the stall completely disappears.

Does the x86 MOV instruction used by std::memory_order_release force a partial or full drain of the WC Buffers to satisfy C++ release semantics, or does the stall occur because a subsequent std::memory_order_relaxed load triggers an internal CPU pipeline flush due to a false memory dependency alias across the Store Buffer and Fill Buffer boundaries?

#     this when you receive I/O errors because of the standard approach where
#     mod_ssl sends the close notify alert.

items.title: Check whenever a file gets changed
items.body:
I have an idea to secure my application data (a .json file), but I'm not sure if it's the best approach or how to implement it in C++.

My goal is to create a file that only my program can access, protecting it from being opened, modified, or deleted by users or other apps at all time, even when my program is not running.

To handle synchronization, my current theory is: instead of constantly downloading the file from the server (which causes bad performance), the app could just check the file's integrity on launch. If the file was somehow changed while the app was closed, the program would overwrite it with a fresh copy from the server. Otherwise, it uses the local file and pushes updates to the server when needed.

Is this flow a good practice, or is there a better way to achieve this in C++?

items.title: How to implement 1:N fingerprint identification using DigitalPersona SDK in C#?
items.body:
I am building a .NET application for a university project that requires 1:N (one-to-many) fingerprint identification using a DigitalPersona scanner.

I have successfully implemented 1:1 verification using the DPFP.Verification.Verification class, but I cannot figure out how to scale this to 1:N matching to find a user from a database of registered fingerprints.

My Question: Does the DigitalPersona .NET SDK have a built-in DPFP.Identification class or a specific driver/API call meant for 1:N matching rather than looping through 1:1 verifications?

If so, how should the SDK be configured to perform a proper 1:N identification search?

I am currently iterating through a list of stored DPFP.Template objects and running the 1:1 verification against each one, but this feels highly inefficient and slow.

// My current inefficient 1:N approach
foreach (var storedUser in UserDatabase)
{
    var result = verification.Verify(features, storedUser.Template, ref fAResult);
    if (result.Verified)
    {
        MessageBox.Show("Match found: " + storedUser.Name);
        break;
    }
}

#include <stdio.h>
#include <sys/types.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <netinet/in.h>
#include <netdb.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>

#include <fcntl.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>

#define SERVER_PORT     710
#define MAX_PENDING     5
#define MAX_LINE        512

int main() {
    struct sockaddr_in sin;
    char buf[MAX_LINE];
    int buf_len;
    socklen_t addr_len;
    int s, new_s;
    
    int fd;
    char *myfifo = "/tmp/myfifo";

    /* build address data structure */
    bzero((char *)&sin, sizeof(sin));
    sin.sin_family = AF_INET;
    sin.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;

        exit(1);
    }
    listen(s, MAX_PENDING);
    
    mkfifo(myfifo, 0666);
    fd = open(myfifo, O_WRONLY);

    /* wait for connection, then receive and print text */
    while (1) {
        if ((new_s = accept(s, (struct sockaddr *)&sin, &addr_len)) < 0) {
            perror("simplex-talk: accept");
            exit(1);
        }
        while (buf_len = recv(new_s, buf, sizeof(buf), 0)) {
            //fputs(buf, stdout);
            write(fd, buf, sizeof(buf));
        }
        close(new_s);
    }
    close(fd);
}

items.title: How can I validate a specific field in a JSON response using Postman?
items.body:
I'm testing a REST API using Postman and want to verify that a specific field in the JSON response contains the expected value.

For example, the API returns this response:

{
  "id": 101,
  "name": "Test User",
  "status": "active"
}

I want to check that the status field equals "active" and that the id field equals 101.

How can I write a Postman test script to validate these values? Also, how can I make the test fail if either value is incorrect? The test should pass when both values match and fail when either value is different.

items.title: How can I disable code completion in comments in Intellij (Android Studio)?
items.body:
I use code completion all the time (don't we all!). But code completion does not make sense when in the middle of a comment.

For example, I tried to type:

/** 
 * This function blah blah blah and uses the following state
 *
 *    MyState.START
 *
 * etc...
 */

But by hitting the enter button at the end of the word "state", code-complete thought I was writing a stateflow (I'm using Android Studio was documenting my code and typed the word "state", but what came out was:

/**
 * This function blah blah blah and uses the following private val _ MutableStateFlow<>()
val = _.asStateFlow()
 *
 */

within my kdoc comment.

This and many other chunks of code are suggested while writing comments. I can disable code completion, but that will seriously slow down my work (I use the stateflow code completion almost every day, so I don't want to disable that). The IDE definitely knows I'm in a comment as the color of my typing is comment color.

Yes, I can turn off spelling check and grammar check within comments. But how do you disable code-complete within comments?

items.title: How do I accurately detect gamepad button presses in JavaScript?
items.body:
I'm building a browser-based FPS game and I want to include gamepad/xbox controller support.

The common method to detect gamepad button presses is to just use polling with requestAnimationFrame:

function poll() {
  let gamepads = navigator.getGamepads();
  if (gamepads.length > 0) {
    let gamepad = gamepads[0];
    if (gamepad.buttons[0].pressed) {
      console.log("Button 'A' pressed!");
    }
  }
  requestAnimationFrame(poll);
}
poll();

The problem with this method is that, if there is a large drop in framerate (such as a sudden freeze), the user will be able to press a button once or multiple times, which will go undetected while the freeze happens. This doesn't just happen with low framerates either. It happens even on devices with high framerates. I notice it especially when I spam a button and the script only detects one or two presses.

How do I detect gamepad button presses as an event listener rather than polling, since that would be more accurate?

        auto resolver = boost::asio::ip::tcp::resolver(ioc);
    
        try {
            
            std::cout << "getRequest resolver created.\n";
    
            boost::asio::ssl::stream<boost::asio::ip::tcp::socket> stream{ ioc, ssl_ctx };
            std::cout << "getRequest stream created.\n";
    
            auto f_hostResolvedResults = resolver.async_resolve(host, "https", boost::asio::use_future);
    
            std::cout << "getRequest resolve started.\n";
    
            auto hostResolvedResults = f_hostResolvedResults.get();
            std::cout << "getRequest got resolve results.\n";
    
            if (hostResolvedResults.empty()) {
                const std::string msg{ "HTTP REQUEST. No resolve results for " + host + ".\n" };
                std::cerr << msg;
                ioc.stop();
                return std::move(HttpResponse(false, -1, std::move(msg)));
            }
    
            boost::asio::ip::tcp::endpoint resolved = *(hostResolvedResults.cbegin());
    
            std::cout << "getRequest resolved. " << resolved << "\n";
            
            boost::asio::ip::tcp::socket::lowest_layer_type& ll_socket = stream.lowest_layer();
            boost::asio::ip::tcp::no_delay option(true);
    
            auto f_connect = boost::asio::async_connect(ll_socket, hostResolvedResults, boost::asio::use_future);
    
            std::cout << getCurrentTimeString() << " getRequest Waiting connect...\n";
    
            f_connect.get();
    
            std::cout << getCurrentTimeString() << " getRequest Connected.\n";
    
            boost::certify::set_server_hostname(stream, host, ec);
            if (ec) {
                const std::string msg{ "HTTP REQUEST. Error setting server hostname for " + host + ": " + ec.what() + "\n" };
                std::cerr << msg;
                ioc.stop();
                return std::move(HttpResponse(false, -1, std::move(msg)));
            }
    
            std::cout << "getRequest " << step++ << "\n";
    
            boost::certify::sni_hostname(stream, host, ec);
            if (ec) {
                const std::string msg{ "HTTP REQUEST. Error setting SNI hostname on SSL stream for " + host + ": " + ec.what() + "\n" };
                std::cerr << msg;
                ioc.stop();
                return std::move(HttpResponse(false, -1, std::move(msg)));
            }
    
            std::cout << "getRequest " << step++ << "\n";
    
            auto f_handshake = stream.async_handshake(boost::asio::ssl::stream_base::client, boost::asio::use_future);
            std::cout << "getRequest start handshake\n";
    
            f_handshake.get();
            std::cout << "getRequest handshake ok" << "\n";
    
            // Create HTTP request
            http::request<http::empty_body> req;
            req.version(11);
            req.method(http::verb::get);
            req.target(query);
            req.set(http::field::host, host);
    
            req.prepare_payload();
    
            std::cout << "getRequest " << step++ << "\n";
    
            auto f_write = boost::beast::http::async_write(stream, req, boost::asio::use_future);
            std::cout << "getRequest write started\n";
    
            auto write = f_write.get();
            std::cout << getCurrentTimeString() << " getRequest write ok. " << write << " bytes." << "\n";
    
            // Receive the response
            boost::beast::flat_buffer buffer;
            http::response<http::string_body> res;
            std::future<std::size_t> f_bytesRead = http::async_read(stream, buffer, res, boost::asio::use_future);
            std::cout << getCurrentTimeString() << " getRequest read start\n";
    
            // check read timeout
            auto readTimeout = f_bytesRead.wait_for(3s);
    
            if (readTimeout != std::future_status::ready) {
    
                const auto futureValid = f_bytesRead.valid();
                std::cout << getCurrentTimeString() << " future is valid: " << futureValid << "\n";
    
                if (futureValid) {
                    std::cout << getCurrentTimeString() << " read retry\n";
                    f_bytesRead = http::async_read(stream, buffer, res, boost::asio::use_future);
                    readTimeout = f_bytesRead.wait_for(2s);
                }
    
                if (readTimeout != std::future_status::ready) {
    
                    const std::string msg = getCurrentTimeString() + " getRequest read timeout\n";
                    std::cout << msg;
                    ioc.stop();
                    return std::move(HttpResponse(false, -1, std::move(msg)));
    
                }
    
            }
            const size_t bytesRead = f_bytesRead.get();
    
            std::cout << getCurrentTimeString() << " getRequest read ok. " << bytesRead << " bytes." << "\n";
    
            // Shut down the SSL stream
    
            std::latch m_shutdownLatch{1};
            auto shutdownCompletitionHandler { [&](boost::beast::error_code shutdownEC) {
                    ec = shutdownEC;
                    std::cout << getCurrentTimeString() << " getRequest shutdown completition handler: " << shutdownEC.what() << "\n";
                    m_shutdownLatch.count_down();
                }
            }; 
    
            stream.async_shutdown(shutdownCompletitionHandler);
            std::cout << "getRequest shutdown start\n";
    
            m_shutdownLatch.wait();
    
            std::cout << "getRequest shutdown finish\n";
    
            if (ec && ec != boost::asio::ssl::error::stream_truncated) {
                const std::string msg = "HTTP REQUEST. Error shutting down SSL stream: " + ec.what() + "\n";
                std::cerr << msg;
                ioc.stop();
                return std::move(HttpResponse(false, -1, std::move(msg)));
            }
    
            std::cout << "getRequest " << step++ << "\n";
    
            // Parse and return the response body as JSON
            ioc.stop();
            return std::move(HttpResponse(true, 0, res.body()));
    
        } catch (std::runtime_error& e) {
    
            const std::string msg{ "(boost) Request "s + query + " failed: "s + e.what() };
            ioc.stop();
            return std::move(HttpResponse(false, -1, std::move(msg)));
    
        } catch (const std::exception& e) {
    
            const std::string msg{ "(not boost) Request "s + query + " failed: "s + e.what() };
            ioc.stop();
            return std::move(HttpResponse(false, -1, std::move(msg)));
    
        }
    
    } // const HttpResponse getRequest(const std::string& host, const std::string& query)
    
    const HttpResponse getRequest(std::string const& host, std::string const& query) {
        boost::asio::io_context ioc;
        auto work_guard = boost::asio::make_work_guard(ioc);
    
        auto result { std::async(std::launch::async, [&]() -> const HttpResponse { return m_getRequest(ioc, host, query); }) };
        // auto result = m_getRequest(ioc, host, query);
        std::cout << "asnyc started\n";
    
        ioc.run();
    
        auto rv = result.get();
        std::cout << "got result\n";
    
        return rv;
    }
    
    int main() {
        const std::string host {"api-demo.bybit.com"};
    
        const std::string getInstrumentsInfoBase = "/v5/market/instruments-info?category=option&baseCoin=";
    
        const std::array<std::string, 16> baseCoins {"SNDK", "SOXL", "QQQ", "DOGE", "XRP", "MU", "TSLA", "BTC", "SPCX", "MNT", "ETH", "SOL", "HYPE", "XAUT", "NVDA", "SKHY"};
    
        int count {0};
        for(auto baseCoin : baseCoins) {
    
            auto res = getRequest(host, getInstrumentsInfoBase + baseCoin);
    
            if (res.success) {
                std::cout << baseCoin << " instruments got.\n";
                count++;
            } else {
                std::cout << baseCoin << " error retrieving instruments info: " << res.content << std::endl;
                break;
            }
    
        }
    
        std::cout << "Received " << count << " of " << baseCoins.size() << " instruments info.\n";
    
        return 0;
    }

Here are debug messages:

2026-10-10 14:44:06.807568512 future is valid: true
2026-10-10 14:44:06.807647529 read retry
2026-10-10 14:44:08.807821793 getRequest read timeout

This code sends 17 requests maximum, one-by-one. Every time calling caller wrapper with creating new instance of io_context. Sometimes all 17 requests are working fine, sometime on a random request I'm catching "timeout".

P.S. The most strange thing for me here is that when I'm getting a timeout I see with tcpdmp that response arrives with same regular typical delivery delay as for previous successful requests.

UPDATE. Today I made some changes:

  • previously that software was running on a single vCPU VM (Debian 13.7 on bare-metal ESXi 7). I added second vCPU.
  • also added TCP_NODELAY:

    stream.lowest_layer().set_option(boost::asio::ip::tcp::no_delay(true));

Since that no any occasional stalls. Thanks to everyone (except stupid AI).

items.title: How can a Spring Security OAuth2 failure handler access the token used by the failed request?
items.body:
My custom OAuth2AuthorizationFailureHandler can load the current cached token, but I need the token used by the request that failed so that invalidation does not remove its replacement. These can differ when a replacement is stored while a request is in flight.

In a non-servlet client_credentials application, concurrent callers share an OAuth2ClientHttpRequestInterceptor, a client registration and a principal. The ordering I need to handle is:

  1. A resource request is sent with T1.
  2. Another caller stores T2 for the same registration/principal while that request is in flight.
  3. The request using T1 receives 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token".

I tried a custom handler that loads the OAuth2AuthorizedClient from the service. This deterministic example shows its inputs; the handler only logs them and does not remove anything. The execution stub models step 2 before returning the 401, without threads or external servers.

Tested with Java 21, Spring Security 7.1.1 and Spring Framework 7.0.9. Dependencies: spring-security-oauth2-client:7.1.1, spring-web:7.0.9, spring-test:7.0.9, jakarta.servlet-api:6.1.0 and their transitive dependencies.

import java.net.URI;
import java.time.Instant;

import org.springframework.http.*;
import org.springframework.mock.http.client.MockClientHttpRequest;
import org.springframework.mock.http.client.MockClientHttpResponse;
import org.springframework.security.authentication.TestingAuthenticationToken;
import org.springframework.security.core.Authentication;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.client.*;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.client.registration.*;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.client.web.client.OAuth2ClientHttpRequestInterceptor;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.core.*;

public class Late401CustomHandler {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        var registration = ClientRegistration.withRegistrationId("demo")
                .clientId("demo").clientSecret("unused")
                .authorizationGrantType(AuthorizationGrantType.CLIENT_CREDENTIALS)
                .tokenUri("https://issuer.invalid/token").build();
        Authentication principal = new TestingAuthenticationToken("service", "unused");
        var service = new InMemoryOAuth2AuthorizedClientService(
                new InMemoryClientRegistrationRepository(registration));
        service.saveAuthorizedClient(client(registration, "T1"), principal);

        // Use the cached client so the example needs no token endpoint.
        OAuth2AuthorizedClientManager manager = request ->
                service.loadAuthorizedClient("demo", principal.getName());
        var interceptor = new OAuth2ClientHttpRequestInterceptor(manager);
        interceptor.setClientRegistrationIdResolver(request -> "demo");
        interceptor.setPrincipalResolver(request -> principal);
        interceptor.setAuthorizationFailureHandler((error, authentication, attributes) -> {
            OAuth2AuthorizedClient current =
                    service.loadAuthorizedClient("demo", authentication.getName());
            System.out.println("failure=" + error.getError().getErrorCode());
            System.out.println("cached=" + current.getAccessToken().getTokenValue());
            System.out.println("attributeKeys=" + attributes.keySet());
        });

        var request = new MockClientHttpRequest(HttpMethod.GET,
                URI.create("https://resource.invalid/data"));
        interceptor.intercept(request, new byte[0], (sent, body) -> {
            System.out.println("sent=" + sent.getHeaders().getFirst(HttpHeaders.AUTHORIZATION));
            // Model another caller storing T2 while the request using T1 is in flight.
            service.saveAuthorizedClient(client(registration, "T2"), principal);
            var response = new MockClientHttpResponse(new byte[0], HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED);
            response.getHeaders().set(HttpHeaders.WWW_AUTHENTICATE,
                    "Bearer error=\"invalid_token\"");
            return response;
        }).close();
    }

    private static OAuth2AuthorizedClient client(ClientRegistration registration, String token) {
        Instant now = Instant.now();
        return new OAuth2AuthorizedClient(registration, "service",
                new OAuth2AccessToken(OAuth2AccessToken.TokenType.BEARER,
                        token, now.minusSeconds(1), now.plusSeconds(3600)));
    }
}

Output:

sent=Bearer T1
failure=invalid_token
cached=T2
attributeKeys=[]

Reading the authorized client inside the handler therefore gives me T2, not the token T1 used by the failed request. In the 7.1.1 interceptor source, handleAuthorizationFailure creates a new attributes map and adds servlet request/response objects only when a servlet request context exists. In this non-servlet example the map is empty.

How should I carry the failed request's bearer token into the failure callback so the store can atomically remove only the matching token? A wrapper or another extension point is acceptable. I want to preserve invalidation when the cached token matches the failed request, while retaining T2 when a late failure belongs to T1, without serializing complete resource requests.

items.title: Why does a LAG offset just above INT32 max leak the LongColumn class name?
items.body:
An inspection-history endpoint accepts the number of samples to look back. While testing the configuration boundary on Apache IoTDB 2.0.10 table model, offset 2147483648 returned an internal column type name instead of an argument-range error.

The first thing I noticed was this result:

SELECT time,reading,LAG(reading,2147483648) OVER (PARTITION BY line ORDER BY time) AS prior FROM inspection_readings ORDER BY time;

Msg: org.apache.iotdb.jdbc.IoTDBSQLException: 301: org.apache.tsfile.read.common.block.column.LongColumn

For a reproducible example, these are the schema and original data:

CREATE TABLE inspection_readings (line STRING TAG, reading INT32 FIELD);
INSERT INTO inspection_readings(time,line,reading) VALUES (1000,'line-a',10),(2000,'line-a',20),(3000,'line-a',30);

I then used control with only the offset changed to 1 as a control:

SELECT time,reading,LAG(reading,1) OVER (PARTITION BY line ORDER BY time) AS prior FROM inspection_readings ORDER BY time;

+-----------------------------+-------+-----+
|                         time|reading|prior|
+-----------------------------+-------+-----+
|1970-01-01T08:00:01.000+08:00|     10| null|
|1970-01-01T08:00:02.000+08:00|     20|   10|
|1970-01-01T08:00:03.000+08:00|     30|   20|
+-----------------------------+-------+-----+

Must a window offset fit in INT32? If so, why does 2.0.10 leak org.apache.tsfile.read.common.block.column.LongColumn instead of returning a user-facing argument error?

items.title: Relay Broadcasting in lua for game systems
items.body:
I'm working on a love2d project and I'm trying to implement a game mechanic with the following functional description and pseudocode:

Iterate over all systems in the galaxyData table. For each system, send a message out to neighbours via a temporary table. Once iterated over the whole of the galaxy, reconcile the old messages table with the new messages table and clear the temporary table. Before sending messages, confirm there are no duplicates so the relay data doesn't grow.

for systems in galaxy do
    for neighbour in systems do
        neighbour.messages.temp[system.name] = system.status
    end
end
for systems in galaxy do
    for existingMessages in systems do
        if existingMessage.age > system.messages.temp.age then
           existingMessage = system.messages.temp
        end
    end
    system.messages.temp = {}
end

The issue that I'm having is when the messages change. Right now, the original message will propagate through the entire network, but it runs into two problems that stops the rest of the process where:

  • At the first broadcast after updating, one of the neighbours is left out of the updated message sent in the first for loop. In the below output, "guwinmal" is a neighbour to "yuggera" but isn't including in the first iteraton post update
different ages  nguri   yuggera 6
different ages  byellee yuggera 6
different ages  yuwi    yuggera 7
different ages  guwinmal        yuggera 7
different ages  darumbal        yuggera 7
  • When the signals reach a "bottleneck" system, the message stops propagating. In this output, there should be another 2 iterations at 9 & 10, but the signals further down seem to be "reflecting" and killing my broadcast.
different ages  nguri   yuggera 6
different ages  byellee yuggera 6
different ages  yuwi    yuggera 7
different ages  guwinmal        yuggera 7
different ages  darumbal        yuggera 7
different ages  gurenggureng    yuggera 8

So, long story short, has anyone messed around with systems like this and have any tips? This is going to be a core mechanic of the game.

items.title: Does loadTable().to_pandas() transfer all data or only metadata first?
items.body:
When using the Python API, I want to understand the data transfer behavior of loadTable vs to_pandas. The database table has millions of rows and I don't want to accidentally trigger a full transfer.

import dolphindb as ddb

s = ddb.session()
s.connect("localhost", 8848, "admin", "123456")

# Does this already pull data?
t = s.loadTable("dfs://stock_db", "tick")

# Or does the actual transfer happen here?
df = t.to_pandas()

What I'm really asking: does loadTable() return a lazy reference (metadata/handle only), or does it eagerly fetch some or all data? If I chain a filter before to_pandas(), is the filter pushed down to the server, or does it first transfer everything and then filter client-side?

df = s.loadTable("dfs://stock_db", "tick").select("sym", "price").where("date=2025.01.01").to_pandas()

static void doFighters(void)
{
    Laser *e, *prev;

    prev = &stage.fighterHead;

    for (e = stage.fighterHead.next; e != NULL; e = e->next)
    {
        e->x += e->dx;
        e->y += e->dy;

        if (e != player && e->x < -e->w)
        {
            e->health <= 0;
        }

        if (e->health == 0)
        {
            if (e == player)
            {
                player = NULL;
            }

            if (e == stage.fighterTail)
            {
                stage.fighterTail = prev;
            }

            prev->next = e->next;
            delete e;
            e = prev;
        }

        prev = e;
    }
}

        if (dot.keyboard[SDL_SCANCODE_LEFT])

            player->dx = -PLAYER_SPEED;

void calcScope(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2, float *dx, float *dy)
{
int steps = MAX(abs(x1 - x2), abs(y1 - y2));

if (steps == 0)
{
*dx = *dy = 0;
return;
}

*dx = (x1 - x2);
*dx /= steps;

*dy = (y1 - y2);
*dy /= steps;
}

static void fireAlienBullet(Laser *e)

    bullet->x += (e->w / 2) - (bullet->w / 2);

    calcSlope(player->x + (player->w / 2), player->y + (player->h / 2), e->x, e->y, &bullet->dx, &bullet->dy);

    bullet->dx *= ALIEN_BULLET_SPEED;

void calcSlope(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2, float *dx, float *dy)
{
    int steps = MAX(abs(x1 - x2), abs(y1 - y2));

    if (steps == 0)
    {
        *dx = *dy = 0;
        return;
    }

    *dx = (x1 - x2);
    *dx /= steps;

    *dy = (y1 - y2);
    *dy /= steps;
}

void blitRect(SDL_Texture *texture, SDL_Rect *src, int x, int y)
{
SDL_Rect dest;

dest.x = x;
dest.y = y;
dest.w = src->w;
dest.h = src->h;

SDL_RenderCopy(gRenderer, texture, src, &dest);

}
static void doExplosions(void)
{
Explosion *e, *prev;

prev = &stage.explosionHead;

for (e = stage.explosionHead.next ; e != NULL ; e = e->next)
{
    e->x += e->dx;
    e->y += e->dy;

    if(--e->a <= 0)
    {
        if(e == stage.explosionTail)
        {
        stage.explosionTail = prev;
        }

    prev->next = e->next;
    delete e;
    e = prev;
}

prev = e;
}
}

static void doDebris(void)
{
Debris *d, *prev;

prev = &stage.debrisHead;

for(d = stage.debrisHead.next ; d != NULL; d = d->next)
{
    d->x += d->dx;
    d->y += d->dy;

    d->dy += 0.5;

if (--d->life <= 0)
{
    if(d == stage.debrisTail)
    {
        stage.debrisTail = prev;
    }

    prev->next = d->next;
    delete d;
    d = prev;
}
prev = d;
}
}

static void addExplosions(int x, int y, int num)
{
    Explosion *e;
    int        i;

    for (i = 0; i < num; i++)
    {
        e = new Explosion();
        stage.explosionTail->next = e;
        stage.explosionTail = e;

        e->x = x + (rand() % 32) - (rand() % 32);
        e->y = y + (rand() % 32) - (rand() % 32);
        e->dx = (rand() % 10) - (rand() % 10);
        e->dy = (rand() % 10) - (rand() % 10);

        e->dx /= 10;
        e->dy /= 10;

        switch (rand() % 4)
        {
            case 0:
                e->r = 255;
                break;

            case 1:
                e->r = 255;
                e->g = 128;
                break;

            case 2:
                e->r = 255;
                e->g = 255;
                break;

            default:
                e->r = 255;
                e->g = 255;
                e->b = 255;
                break;
        }

        e->a = rand() % FPS * 3;
    }
}

static void addDebris(Laser *e)
{
    Debris *d;
    int     x, y, w, h;

    w = e->w / 2;
    h = e->h / 2;

    for (y = 0; y <= h; y += h)
    {
        for (x = 0; x <= w; x += w)
        {
            d = new Debris();
            stage.debrisTail->next = d;
            stage.debrisTail = d;

            d->x = e->x + e->w / 2;
            d->y = e->y + e->h / 2;
            d->dx = (rand() % 5) - (rand() % 5);
            d->dy = -(5 + (rand() % 12));
            d->life = FPS * 2;
            d->texture = e->texture;

            d->rect.x = x;
            d->rect.y = y;
            d->rect.w = w;
            d->rect.h = h;
        }
    }
}

void drawTextEH(int x, int y, int r, int g, int b, int align, char *format, ...)
{
    int      i, len, c;
    SDL_Rect rect;
    va_list  args;

    memset(&drawTextBuffer, '\0', sizeof(drawTextBuffer));

    va_start(args, format);
    vsprintf(drawTextBuffer, format, args);
    va_end(args);

    len = strlen(drawTextBuffer);

    switch (align)
    {
        case TEXT_RIGHT:
            x -= (len * GLYPH_WIDTH);
            break;

        case TEXT_CENTER:
            x -= (len * GLYPH_WIDTH) / 2;
            break;
    }

    rect.w = GLYPH_WIDTH;
    rect.h = GLYPH_HEIGHT;
    rect.y = 0;

    SDL_SetTextureColorMod(fontTexture, r, g, b);

    for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
    {
        c = drawTextBuffer[i];

        if (c >= ' ' && c <= 'Z')
        {
            rect.x = (c - ' ') * GLYPH_WIDTH;

            blitRect(fontTexture, &rect, x, y);

            x += GLYPH_WIDTH;

static void doPointsPods(void)
{
    Laser *e, *prev;

    prev = &stage.pointsHead;

    for (e = stage.pointsHead.next; e != NULL; e = e->next)
    {
        if (e->x < 0)
        {
            e->x = 0;
            e->dx = -e->dx;
        }

        if (e->x + e->w > SCREEN_WIDTH)
        {
            e->x = SCREEN_WIDTH - e->w;
            e->dx = -e->dx;
        }

        if (e->y < 0)
        {
            e->y = 0;
            e->dy = -e->dy;
        }

        if (e->y + e->h > SCREEN_HEIGHT)
        {
            e->y = SCREEN_HEIGHT - e->h;
            e->dy = -e->dy;
        }

        e->x += e->dx;
        e->y += e->dy;

        if (player != NULL && collision(e->x, e->y, e->w, e->h, player->x, player->y, player->w, player->h))
        {
            e->health = 0;

            stage.score++;

            highscore = MAX(stage.score, highscore);

            playSound(SND_POINTS, CH_POINTS);
        }

        if (--e->health <= 0)
        {
            if (e == stage.pointsTail)
            {
                stage.pointsTail = prev;
            }

            prev->next = e->next;
            free(e);
            e = prev;
        }

        prev = e;
    }
}

static void addPointsPod(int x, int y)
{
    Laser *e;

    e = new Laser();
    stage.pointsTail->next = e;
    stage.pointsTail = e;

    e->x = x;
    e->y = y;
    e->dx = -(rand() % 5);
    e->dy = (rand() % 5) - (rand() % 5);
    e->health = FPS * 10;
    e->texture = pointsTexture;

    SDL_QueryTexture(e->texture, NULL, NULL, &e->w, &e->h);

    e->x -= e->w / 2;
    e->y -= e->h / 2;
}

static void drawPointsPods(void)
{

    for (e = stage.pointsHead.next; e != NULL; e = e->next)

    }

        y += 50;

void addHighscore(int score)
{
    Highscore newHighscores[NUM_HIGHSCORES + 1];
    int       i;

    memset(newHighscores, 0, sizeof(Highscore) * (NUM_HIGHSCORES + 1));

    for (i = 0; i < NUM_HIGHSCORES; i++)
    {
        newHighscores[i] = highscores.highscore[i];
        newHighscores[i].recent = 0;
    }

    newHighscores[NUM_HIGHSCORES].score = score;
    newHighscores[NUM_HIGHSCORES].recent = 1;

    qsort(newHighscores, NUM_HIGHSCORES + 1, sizeof(Highscore), highscoreComparator);

    newHighscore = NULL;

    for (i = 0; i < NUM_HIGHSCORES; i++)
    {
        highscores.highscore[i] = newHighscores[i];

        if (highscores.highscore[i].recent)
        {
            newHighscore = &highscores.highscore[i];
        }
    }
}
static int highscoreComparator(const void *a, const void *b)

    Highscore *h1 = ((Highscore*)a);
    Highscore *h2 = ((Highscore*)b);

    return h2->score - h1->score;

    drawText(SCREEN_WIDTH / 2, 250, 128, 255, 128, TEXT_CENTER, newHighscore->name);

    if (cursorBlink < FPS / 2)
    {

static void capFrameRate(long *then, float *remainder)
{
    long wait, frameTime;

    wait = 16 + *remainder;

    *remainder -= (int)*remainder;

    frameTime = SDL_GetTicks() - *then;

    wait -= frameTime;

    if (wait < 1)
    {
        wait = 1;
    }

    SDL_Delay(wait);

    *remainder += 0.667;

    *then = SDL_GetTicks();
}

void cleanup(void)

    SDL_DestroyRenderer(dot.renderer);

    SDL_DestroyWindow(dot.window);

    SDL_Quit();
}

items.title: Apps Script web apps return 302 → 404 on one Samsung Android device, but works on other devices
items.body:
I'm experiencing an unusual issue accessing deployed Google Apps Script web applications on my Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8.

Problem:

Multiple Apps Script web applications deployed with "Execute as: Me" and "Who has access: Anyone" fail to open on my phone, displaying Google's "Sorry, unable to open the file at this time" error.

Testing performed:

  • Windows PC using Microsoft Edge: Works, HTTP 200.

  • Windows PC using Edge InPrivate: Works, HTTP 200.

  • iPad using Safari: Works.

  • Another person's Android phone: Works.

  • My Galaxy Z Fold 8 using Chrome, Firefox, Samsung Internet, and Edge: Fails.

  • Chrome inside Samsung Secure Folder, including while signed out of Google: Fails.

  • Wi-Fi and cellular connections: Both fail.

  • Cleared Google site cookies, updated phone software, and restarted: No improvement.

  • Google Apps Script dashboard (script.google.com/home): Works normally.

Chrome DevTools findings:

When opening the account-neutral deployment URL:

https://script.google.com/macros/s/DEPLOYMENT_ID/exec

Google returns:

  1. HTTP 302 redirect to /macros/u/2/s/DEPLOYMENT_ID/exec

  2. HTTP 404 Not Found at the redirected address.

Manually accessing /macros/u/0/s/DEPLOYMENT_ID/exec also returns HTTP 404.

On my Windows PC, the account-neutral /macros/s/DEPLOYMENT_ID/exec request returns HTTP 200 and the application loads successfully.

The HTTP 404 response contains Google's generic Drive "Page Not Found" HTML.

Question:

What could cause Google Apps Script deployment URLs to return HTTP 404 on one Android device while working on other devices, including another Android phone? Is there a known issue with account-specific routing or Google authentication on Android?

items.title: AImageReader -> Sampling swaps RGB <-> BGR, how to fix?
items.body:
I use an AImageReader and a Vulkan sampler to sample the camera image in a shader, used in an AR application. I have two problems:

  1. Using the format AIMAGE_FORMAT_PRIVATE does not reliably work across all devices (because some devices apply some proprietary compressed format which just lead to garbage when being sampled).

  2. Format AIMAGE_FORMAT_YUV_420_888 is the only format that must be supported by all devices according to the documentation in NdkImage.h and indeed, this works across all devices I've tested. However, blue and red color channels are swapped on Adreno devices, i.e. RGB↔BGR and I have no idea how to establish correct sampling.

Here's my setup:

// 1) Camera stream
AImageReader_newWithUsage(w, h, format /* AIMAGE_FORMAT_PRIVATE or AIMAGE_FORMAT_YUV_420_888 */, AHARDWAREBUFFER_USAGE_GPU_SAMPLED_IMAGE, maxImages, &reader);
// per frame: AImageReader_acquireLatestImage -> AImage_getHardwareBuffer(image, &ahb)


// 2) Conversion + immutable sampler, from the first frame's properties
VkAndroidHardwareBufferFormatPropertiesANDROID formatInfo  {
    .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_ANDROID_HARDWARE_BUFFER_FORMAT_PROPERTIES_ANDROID,
    .pNext = nullptr
};
VkAndroidHardwareBufferPropertiesANDROID propertiesInfo {
    .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_ANDROID_HARDWARE_BUFFER_PROPERTIES_ANDROID,
    .pNext = &formatInfo
};

auto res = vkGetAndroidHardwareBufferPropertiesANDROID(device, buffer, &propertiesInfo);
if (res != VK_SUCCESS) {
    // error handling
}

VkExternalFormatANDROID externalFormat {
    .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_EXTERNAL_FORMAT_ANDROID,
    .pNext = nullptr,
    .externalFormat = formatInfo.externalFormat
};
VkSamplerYcbcrConversionCreateInfo convInfo {
    .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_SAMPLER_YCBCR_CONVERSION_CREATE_INFO,
    .pNext = &externalFormat,
    .format = formatInfo.format,
    // Manual YCbCr conversion in shader
    .ycbcrModel = VK_SAMPLER_YCBCR_MODEL_CONVERSION_YCBCR_IDENTITY,
    .ycbcrRange = formatInfo.suggestedYcbcrRange,
    .components = formatInfo.samplerYcbcrConversionComponents,

items.title: Why do POSIX and the C FAQ suggest casting char ** to const char * const *?
items.body:
It is established in ISO/IEC 9899:2018 that an implicit assignment of a char ** (such as the address of a char *) to a const char ** is unsafe, and its reasoning is explicitly illustrated in §6.5.16.2, p. 74, ¶6:

EXAMPLE 3 Consider the fragment:

const char **cpp;  
char *p;  
const char c = 'A';

cpp = &p; // constraint violation  
*cpp = &c; // valid  
*p = 0; // valid

The first assignment is unsafe because it would allow the following valid code to attempt to change the value of the const object c.

Furthermore, in Volume 2 (System Interfaces) of POSIX.1-2024 on p. 875, ¶29858 within the rationale for the exec family of functions, the authors express regret regarding this limitation and note that an explicit cast would be required as a workaround:

Specifying two levels of const−qualification for the argv[ ] and envp[ ] parameters for the exec functions may seem to be the natural choice. [...] Instead, only the array of pointers is noted as constant.

[...]

The only other possibility is the fourth column, but using it would require a cast on the argv or envp arguments.

Similarly, although it lacks normative authority, the comp.lang.c FAQ (Summit, Question 11.10) references the use of such a cast:

In C, if you must assign or pass pointers which have qualifier mismatches at other than the first level of indirection, you must use explicit casts (e.g. (const char **) in this case), although as always, the need for such a cast may indicate a deeper problem which the cast doesn't really fix.

However, while an explicit cast from char ** to const char * const * satisfies the constraints of the cast operator, given that both are scalar (pointer) types, accessing the underlying object through such an lvalue would theoretically result in undefined behavior. According to ISO/IEC 9899:2018, §6.5, p. 55, ¶7:

An object shall have its stored value accessed only by an lvalue expression that has one of the following types.

  • a type compatible with the effective type of the object,

  • a qualifed version of a type compatible with the effective type of the object,

  • a type that is the signed or unsigned type corresponding to the effective type of the object,

  • a type that is the signed or unsigned type corresponding to a qualifed version of the effective type of the object,

  • an aggregate or union type that includes one of the aforementioned types among its members (including, recursively, a member of a subaggregate or contained union), or

  • a character type.

In light of these stipulations, what is the justification for both the POSIX rationale and the comp.lang.c FAQ referencing or suggesting this cast? Is there a nuance or exception within the standard that reconciles this contradiction?

items.title: SwiftUI Custom Layout Subviews: sizeThatFits crashing or returning incorrect frames during multi-pass layout debugging
items.body:
I am implementing a custom layout using SwiftUI’s Layout protocol (SwiftUI.Layout) for a masonry-style wrapping grid. During runtime layout debugging, my custom sizeThatFits(proposal:subviews:cache:) method returns an incorrect bounding size when subviews contain dynamic text wrapped inside a ViewThatFits or asymmetric padding.

When inspecting the layout passes via Xcode's debugger, the proposal width passed down during the second layout pass becomes unspecified (nil), causing my coordinate calculation loop to fall back to zero-width frames and trigger layout constraint warnings in the console:

SwiftUI: Layout invalidation cycle detected. Layout output was unstable across passes.

import SwiftUI

struct MasonryLayout: Layout {
    var spacing: CGFloat = 8

    func sizeThatFits(proposal: ProposedViewSize, subviews: Subviews, cache: inout ()) -> CGSize {
        // Debugging the incoming proposal
        print("Debugging proposal width: \(proposal.width ?? -999)")
        
        let width = proposal.width ?? UIScreen.main.bounds.width
        var totalHeight: CGFloat = 0
        var currentX: CGFloat = 0
        var currentY: CGFloat = 0
        var maxHeightInRow: CGFloat = 0

        for subview in subviews {
            // Measuring subview with explicit child proposal
            let subviewSize = subview.sizeThatFits(.init(width: width - currentX, height: nil))
            
            if currentX + subviewSize.width > width {
                // Move to next row
                currentX = 0
                currentY += maxHeightInRow + spacing
                maxHeightInRow = 0
            }
            
            maxHeightInRow = max(maxHeightInRow, subviewSize.height)
            currentX += subviewSize.width + spacing
        }
        
        totalHeight = currentY + maxHeightInRow
        return CGSize(width: width, height: totalHeight)
    }

    func placeSubviews(in bounds: CGRect, proposal: ProposedViewSize, subviews: Subviews, cache: inout ()) {
        var currentX = bounds.minX
        var currentY = bounds.minY
        var maxHeightInRow: CGFloat = 0

        for subview in subviews {
            let subviewSize = subview.sizeThatFits(.unspecified)
            
            if currentX + subviewSize.width > bounds.maxX {
                currentX = bounds.minX
                currentY += maxHeightInRow + spacing
                maxHeightInRow = 0
            }

            subview.place(
                at: CGPoint(x: currentX, y: currentY),
                proposal: ProposedViewSize(subviewSize)
            )

            maxHeightInRow = max(maxHeightInRow, subviewSize.height)
            currentX += subviewSize.width + spacing
        }
    }
}

1. Why does proposal.width evaluate to nil on subsequent layout passes when embedded inside a scrollable container (ScrollView), and what is the idiomatic way to handle an unspecified proposal width in custom layouts?

2. How can I effectively debug unstable layout passes or layout loops in SwiftUI custom layouts without causing rendering hitches or infinite recursion warnings in the console?

[["id0", "value0"], ["id1", "value1"], ["id2", "value2"] /*, ...*/ ]


Process for variable assignment, manually:

This is just a illustrative example. In a real scenario the variables are in different C++ files, etc.

// ...

std::string var0 = vec[0][1];
int         var1 = std::stoi(vec[1][1]);
int         var2 = std::stoi(vec[2][1]);
// ...

Idea about possible process for variable assignment, manually but friendly because each variable name would have some meaning "connection" to where its value is located:

// ...

std::string var0 = struct1.id0;
int         var1 = struct1.id1;
int         var2 = struct1.id2;
// ...

In this idea, why a struct instead of a map? to not have to manually type the key string. But, if this idea would be a good candidate, then the basic problem in this post keeps being the same at the moment to match/assign the corresponding value from a text file to each variable in the struct, that is the main reason for the present question.


Other options are welcome.


Side notes:

  • The ideal solution would be a process without 3rd-party dependencies.
  • C++23 is welcome.
  • Could this situation be handled in some kind of generic way, that can be easily adapted for other programs, with different variables names and with different file content (with the same file content structure)?

Update with more context:

  • I try to explain and describe everything with plain terms, so, if I don't call anything with its specific terminology is precisely because I'm learning about it and I might not know in depth about it.

  • The configuration file (.txt file) is available at compilation time, so for any update in the configuration file is needed a corresponding update in the program (new file values with their new corresponding variables).

  • As you may have noticed, this post is about the process to load a configuration file, where you have n variables in the program and n corresponding values in a disk file, being n values to assign the n variables. Example with a basic initial way to cover this:

// ...

std::string item0;  // some variable starting with no value

// ...

std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> vec = read_configuration_file(/*...*/);

item0 = vec[0][1];  // alternative: item0 = struct1.id0;

// ...

So, a variable like item0 gets its corresponding value from the line in the file with "id0".

In a situation with just a few variables, this way can work fine because the programmer can easily track and match what file value goes with its corresponding variable, for example, item1 with vec[1][1], item2 with vec[2][1] and so on. But, in a situation with let's say 100 variables to assign each corresponding value with this same way, then the programmer can make mistakes because the simple fact of doing the assignment process manually (error-prone process), manually typing the vec[i][j] part, and if after some update, the file content gets updated and instead of 100 variables and 100 file values now there are 110 variables and 110 file values, with 10 new lines in the configuration file that may be located in any place(in line 40, in line 0, 4 new lines here and 6 lines there, ...), them at the moment to manually update the variables assignment, what previously was var50 = vec[50][1] now needs to be updated with the new value located in vec[55][1], and what previously was var90 = vec[90][1] now needs to be updated with the new value located in vec[99][1], and so on. i.e. a manual process where the programmer can easily mismatch even by maybe 1 single index offset due the need to be manually tracking assignment by assignment, checking 1 by 1 what vec[i][1] goes with its corresponding var_name_x.

So please note the problem I'm looking for a way about how to handle, is the part about manually do the match every variable with its corresponding value that is located in a disk configuration file. About the option to work with a map instead of a vector, unless I'm missing something, I see the main problem is still the same, because in order to have something like item0 = dict["id0"]; you would also need to manually match the key "id0" in the map with what is "id0" in the configuration file (if present, in what line, ...).

A friendly process would be:

  • Some automatic way to map each target variable in the program with its corresponding value in the configuration file (1 value per line).
  • Then being able to do something like std::string var0 = struct1.id0; where the programmer doesn't even need to remember every single exact id name because when you type struct1. the editor auto-complete will show the possible values (which is an incredible useful feature that for example I haven't seen available for maps in C++, of course talking about when the program has the necessary information at compilation time, because with the auto-complete feature you don't need to remember if the id name is specifically dict1["item0"] or if it is dict1["item_0"], etc.).
